F1_no_annotations.capability_note: annotations are OPTIONAL in the MCP Tool object and the stdio transport already ships without them. Zero capability change.

F2_no_property_descriptions.what: F1 + every per-argument description removed; names/types/required kept
F2_no_property_descriptions.capability_note: LOSSY. Per-argument prose is what stops the model inventing argument values. Measured as a bound, not proposed.

F3_empty_schemas.what: F1 + inputSchema emptied; tool descriptions kept
F3_empty_schemas.capability_note: LOSSY - the model no longer knows any argument exists.

F4_names_only_legal.capability_note: THE CATALOG FLOOR. Cheapest legal tools/list for 120 tools. Says nothing about any tool - the model would have to route on the name alone.

F5_bare_name_array.what: a JSON array of the 120 names, nothing else
F5_bare_name_array.capability_note: NOT a tools/list response. Absolute lower bound on putting 120 identifiers on the wire in any form.

verdict.statement: 2,000 is NOT reachable as a flat catalog at 120 tools. The cheapest LEGAL tools/list for 120 tools - every description empty, every schema empty, nothing but names - costs 2919 tokens, which is 919 OVER the ceiling before a single word of description is written. At the floor shape only 81 tools fit under 2,000; at the current average tool shape only 13 do. The ceiling is therefore a statement about tool COUNT, not tool SIZE, and no description- or schema-editing programme can satisfy it while all 120 definitions stay in context. The ceiling IS satisfiable by the deferred surface it was calibrated for: three verbs measure 332 tokens with 1668 to spare.

deferred_surface_definition.name: tool_search
deferred_surface_definition.description: Find SYNAPSE tools by capability. Query in plain language (e.g. 'create a karma render node', 'read USD prim attributes'). Returns matching tool names with one-line summaries. Families: houdini_* (scene/USD/render), synapse_* (memory/routing/solaris), cops_* (Copernicus 2D), tops_* (PDG orchestration). Call this before tool_describe when you do not already know the tool name.

deferred_surface_definition.name: tool_describe
deferred_surface_definition.description: Return the full definition - description and JSON Schema - for one or more SYNAPSE tools by exact name. Call before tool_execute so arguments are built against the real schema rather than guessed.

deferred_surface_definition.name: tool_execute
deferred_surface_definition.description: Invoke a SYNAPSE tool by exact name with arguments matching the schema from tool_describe. Same dispatch spine as the flat surface: undo-wrapped, consent-gated, ledger-recorded.

stats.deferred_note: The three verbs are E1's own construction, written to be realistic rather than flattering - full routing hints in tool_search. They are NOT a proposal (that is E2's call, and it needs E0's cache answer first); they exist so the ceiling is compared against the shape it was actually calibrated for.
